## Overview

This PR runs DiffusionGemma one-step reads in a single forward pass on the CPU backend. It adds `DiffusionConfig.single_pass_reads`, off by default. It is split out of #60527 and holds only the single-pass part.

A one-step read sets `diffusion_read_only` and `diffusion_max_steps=1`. It is the default structured read in examples/features/structured_diffusion. Today it takes two engine steps. The first prefills the prompt and emits nothing. The second runs the canvas. With the flag on, the canvas runs in the step that finishes the prompt.

No other open PR or issue covers this. I searched open PRs for single_pass_reads, single pass diffusion, DiffusionGemma one-step and DiffusionGemma CPU.

I used Claude Code to help with this PR. OpenAI Codex was used for the rebase and validation below. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests below.

## Claims

- On a 44 vCPU Xeon with AMX, one-step reads are **21 to 25% faster for 188-token prompts and 12 to 13% faster for 1250-token prompts**. Reads with a cached prompt prefix are 21% faster.
- Bursts of 4 reads are faster in all 8 shapes when comparing the fastest of 3 bursts per arm: 11 to 14% for 188-token prompts and 3 to 5% for 1250-token prompts. Medians of 3 bursts are noisier, see Validation.
- Constrained reads (`diffusion_constrained`) fuse too, with the same gains.
- Each read takes one engine step instead of two. Over 144 timed calls, engine steps fell from 312 to 168.
- With the flag off, single reads are bit-identical to main.
- With the flag on, outputs are close but not bit-identical. No label decision flipped across 216 reads.
- Reads that request prompt logprobs keep the two-step path.
`single_pass_reads` is rejected on platforms other than CPU, with pipeline parallelism, and with KV connectors or KV offloading.

## Validation

### Rebase validation (2026-10-16)

Rebased onto `9eb7fb9157f622bb2c87839788bbec1d5ef51ad2`. The scheduler conflict with #54627 was resolved by retaining both single-pass canvas registration and upstream's `prefill_admitted` bookkeeping. The feature patch is otherwise unchanged.

Checks on macOS ARM using Python 3.12:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k 'diffusion or SinglePass or prefill_interval or prefill_cadence or throttle' -q` | 40 passed |
| `pytest tests/v1/sample/test_diffusion_gemma_single_pass.py -k 'not TestFusedAttention' tests/test_sampling_params.py -q` | 74 passed, 12 deselected |
| `pytest tests/test_config.py -k single_pass -q` | 6 passed |
| `pre-commit run --from-ref upstream/main --to-ref HEAD` | All applicable hooks passed, including mypy and test tethering |
| `git diff --check upstream/main..HEAD` | Passed |

Hosted pre-commit stopped at the repository authorization gate (three merged PRs and no qualifying label); [the docs preview](https://app.readthedocs.org/projects/vllm/builds/35200241/) stopped because that gate failed. No code checks ran in either hosted job.

The x86 CPU attention cases and end-to-end model benchmarks were not rerun on this host. The CPU and L4 results below are the earlier validation, not measurements on the rebased commit.

### Earlier CPU and GPU validation

Hardware: GCE c3-standard-44, 44 vCPU Intel Xeon Platinum 8481C (AVX-512, AMX), PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu. vLLM built from source at main 6849ca696a with this PR applied. Later changes only shorten the `single_pass_reads` docstring and the README.

google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it in BF16 with LLM.generate and the multiprocess engine, compiled, prefix caching on, `max_num_seqs=16`, `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`, sync scheduling, `diffusion_config={"canvas_length": 64, "single_pass_reads": ...}`. Synthetic chat prompts of 188 and 1250 tokens, canvases of 16 and 32 with a seeded canvas. Per shape: 12 single reads and 3 bursts of 4, the same with `diffusion_constrained`, and 12 cached-prefix reads for the 1250-token prompts. One warmup read and one warmup burst per shape and mode come first. Five arms ran in this order: main, PR flag off, PR flag on, PR flag off again, main again.

Median wall time per call, PR flag off vs on:

| read | flag off | flag on | change | flag off rerun vs flag off |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 188 tokens, canvas 16, 1 read | 0.625 s | 0.466 s | **−25.3%** | −3.6% |
| 188 tokens, canvas 32, 1 read | 0.671 s | 0.504 s | **−24.9%** | −4.2% |
| 1250 tokens, canvas 16, 1 read | 1.126 s | 0.989 s | **−12.2%** | +0.1% |
| 1250 tokens, canvas 32, 1 read | 1.168 s | 1.021 s | **−12.5%** | −0.0% |
| 188 tokens, canvas 16, burst of 4 | 1.352 s | 1.178 s | −12.9% | −0.9% |
| 188 tokens, canvas 32, burst of 4 | 1.732 s | 1.327 s | −23.4% | −14.2% |
| 1250 tokens, canvas 16, burst of 4 | 3.418 s | 3.693 s | +8.1% (see below) | −1.0% |
| 1250 tokens, canvas 32, burst of 4 | 3.527 s | 3.386 s | −4.0% | +5.8% |
| cached prefix, 1250 tokens, canvas 16, 1 read | 0.543 s | 0.425 s | **−21.8%** | −0.4% |
| cached prefix, 1250 tokens, canvas 32, 1 read | 0.582 s | 0.458 s | **−21.2%** | +0.4% |
| constrained, 188 tokens, canvas 16, 1 read | 0.584 s | 0.461 s | **−21.0%** | −5.5% |
| constrained, 188 tokens, canvas 32, 1 read | 0.576 s | 0.440 s | **−23.6%** | +2.0% |
| constrained, 1250 tokens, canvas 16, 1 read | 1.090 s | 0.951 s | **−12.8%** | −0.1% |
| constrained, 1250 tokens, canvas 32, 1 read | 1.101 s | 0.957 s | **−13.0%** | +0.2% |
| constrained, 188 tokens, canvas 16, burst of 4 | 1.219 s | 1.053 s | −13.7% | −2.4% |
| constrained, 188 tokens, canvas 32, burst of 4 | 1.256 s | 1.085 s | −13.6% | +0.2% |
| constrained, 1250 tokens, canvas 16, burst of 4 | 3.290 s | 3.142 s | −4.5% | +0.1% |
| constrained, 1250 tokens, canvas 32, burst of 4 | 3.300 s | 3.149 s | −4.6% | +0.9% |

Each single read saves 0.12 to 0.17 s. The relative gain is smaller for long prompts, where prefill dominates. Burst medians come from 3 bursts each. The offline `LLM` hands a burst to the engine one request at a time. A burst therefore runs as two or three steps with the flag on or off.

The +8.1% on the 1250-token, canvas 16 burst comes from 2 of its 3 flag-on bursts. One ran as a step of 1 read and then a step of 3, and its 3-read step took 3.00 s against 2.27 s for the identical step in another burst. Another ran as 2 reads and then 2. Spreads of 0.5 to 0.8 s between the 3 bursts of one shape occur in every arm, with the flag on or off. The fastest of 3 bursts is the steadier measure, and by that measure every burst shape is faster with the flag on:

| burst of 4 | fastest flag off | fastest flag on | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 188 tokens, canvas 16 | 1.337 s | 1.177 s | −12.0% |
| 188 tokens, canvas 32 | 1.490 s | 1.324 s | −11.1% |
| 1250 tokens, canvas 16 | 3.377 s | 3.264 s | −3.3% |
| 1250 tokens, canvas 32 | 3.524 s | 3.384 s | −4.0% |
| constrained, 188 tokens, canvas 16 | 1.216 s | 1.042 s | −14.3% |
| constrained, 188 tokens, canvas 32 | 1.248 s | 1.079 s | −13.5% |
| constrained, 1250 tokens, canvas 16 | 3.259 s | 3.098 s | −4.9% |
| constrained, 1250 tokens, canvas 32 | 3.292 s | 3.145 s | −4.5% |

Fused bursts spent all but 4 to 9 ms of their wall time inside engine steps.

Startup and memory did not change: 197 s and 63.0 GiB peak RSS with the flag on, 199 s and 62.9 GiB with it off.

With the flag off, the PR matches `main`. Single reads (cold, cached and constrained) are bit-identical to `main`. Bursts differ from `main` by as much as `main` differs from itself. Every latency change is within the spread between repeated runs.

Numerics on the same reads, PR flag on vs off. The parenthesized values compare two flag-off runs. TV distance is between the label distributions renormalized over the 3 label tokens.

| reads | n | identical tokens | label decision flips | top-label logprob shift, mean (sd) / max | label TV, mean / max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 read | 48 | 34 (48) | 0 | +0.029 (0.163) / 0.981 | 0.018 / 0.145 (0 / 0) |
| burst of 4 | 48 | 37 (38) | 0 | +0.005 (0.118) / 0.507 | 0.024 / 0.133 (0.016 / 0.076) |
| cached prefix, 1 read | 24 | 15 (24) | 0 | +0.051 (0.217) / 1.013 | 0.025 / 0.098 (0 / 0) |
| constrained, 1 read | 48 | 32 (48) | 0 | +0.000 (0.023) / 0.090 | 0.012 / 0.074 (0 / 0) |
| constrained, burst of 4 | 48 | 26 (39) | 0 | −0.002 (0.046) / 0.183 | 0.018 / 0.136 (0.015 / 0.134) |

Single reads with the flag off are bit-identical across runs. Their differences come from the fused pass. The worst read moved its top label from 0.86 to 0.71 (1250 tokens, canvas 32). Constrained reads move less than unconstrained ones. The DiffusionGemma `gsm8k` eval runs generation, which this flag does not touch. These read-level comparisons are the accuracy evidence.


Tests on the CPU host above:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `test_diffusion_gemma_single_pass.py` | 19 passed, including 12 fused-attention parity cases on AMX |
| `test_scheduler.py -k "diffusion or SinglePass"` | 27 passed |
| `test_config.py -k single_pass` | 6 passed |
| `test_sampling_params.py` | 67 passed |
| `tests/v1/core` | 1015 passed, 2 failed and 2 errors that also occur on `main` |
| `test_cpu_attn.py -k dynamic_causal` | 36 passed |

The 4 `tests/v1/core` failures are `test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py::test_prefix_cache_hit_rate[base]` and `[mtp]`, and two tests in `test_scheduler_e2e.py` whose engine does not start on CPU. All 4 fail the same way at 6849ca696a without this PR.

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `test_scheduler.py -k "diffusion or SinglePass"` | 26 passed, 1 failed that also fails on `main` |
| `test_scheduler.py`, `test_async_scheduler.py` | 240 passed, 2 failed that also fail on `main` |
| `test_scheduler_e2e.py` | 2 passed |
| `test_diffusion_gemma_single_pass.py` | 7 passed, 12 skipped (CPU attention kernels) |
| `test_diffusion_gemma_reads.py`, `test_diffusion_sampler_stats.py` | 30 passed |
| `test_config.py -k single_pass` | 6 passed |
| `test_sampling_params.py` | 67 passed |

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/sample/test_diffusion_gemma_single_pass.py
pytest -v tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k "diffusion or SinglePass"
pytest -v tests/test_config.py -k single_pass
pytest -v tests/test_sampling_params.py
pytest -v tests/v1/core
pytest -v tests/kernels/attention/test_cpu_attn.py -k dynamic_causal
```

## Details

Design:

- `Scheduler` gets a no-op hook, `_final_prefill_spec_tokens`, called in the running and waiting loops before KV allocation. The core scheduler change is the hook and its two call sites. `DiffusionScheduler` overrides it. It returns one canvas of placeholder draft tokens when the step finishes the prompt of an eligible read, the canvas fits the step's token budget, and the prompt plus canvas stays below `max_model_len`.
- `is_single_pass_read` in `vllm/utils/diffusion.py` is the one eligibility rule. The scheduler uses it to attach the canvas. The sampler uses it to seed the canvas into the draft tokens when the request is added. The two always agree.
- The DiffusionGemma model state splits each fused request into a causal prompt row and a bidirectional canvas row on the same block table. Self-conditioning covers only the canvas rows. The sampler moves fused requests out of the encoder phase in the same step.

Tradeoffs:

- Outputs are not bit-identical with the flag on, which is why it is off by default. The README tells users to validate on their workload first.
- An eligible read waits until the free KV cache holds its prompt and canvas, rather than falling back to two steps.

Limitations:

- CPU only, which is where the fused pass was measured and validated.
- No CI job runs a fused forward pass of the model. `TestFusedAttention` checks the fused attention against two passes on the CPU kernel, in the CPU CI job.
- #60663 batches self-conditioning on the assumption that a request's whole query span is its canvas. A fused request's span also holds the end of its prompt. Whichever PR lands second has to start the canvas at `end - num_logits`.

The 4 `tests/v1/core` failures are `test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py::test_prefix_cache_hit_rate[base]` and `[mtp]`, and two tests in `test_scheduler_e2e.py` whose engine does not start on CPU. All 4 fail the same way at 6849ca696a without this PR.

| `test_scheduler.py -k "diffusion or SinglePass"` | 26 passed, 1 failed that also fails on `main` |
| `test_scheduler.py`, `test_async_scheduler.py` | 240 passed, 2 failed that also fail on `main` |
| `test_scheduler_e2e.py` | 2 passed |
| `test_diffusion_gemma_single_pass.py` | 7 passed, 12 skipped (CPU attention kernels) |
| `test_diffusion_gemma_reads.py`, `test_diffusion_sampler_stats.py` | 30 passed |
| `test_config.py -k single_pass` | 6 passed |
| `test_sampling_params.py` | 67 passed |

Both L4 failures are `test_diffusion_read_deferral_keeps_a_longer_pp_wait` and `test_async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_with_output_placeholders`. Each builds a pipeline-parallel config that `ParallelConfig` rejects on a single-GPU host.

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/sample/test_diffusion_gemma_single_pass.py
pytest -v tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k "diffusion or SinglePass"
pytest -v tests/test_config.py -k single_pass
pytest -v tests/test_sampling_params.py
pytest -v tests/v1/core
pytest -v tests/kernels/attention/test_cpu_attn.py -k dynamic_causal
```

## Details

Design:

- `Scheduler` gets a no-op hook, `_final_prefill_spec_tokens`, called in the running and waiting loops before KV allocation. The core scheduler change is the hook and its two call sites. `DiffusionScheduler` overrides it. It returns one canvas of placeholder draft tokens when the step finishes the prompt of an eligible read, the canvas fits the step's token budget, and the prompt plus canvas stays below `max_model_len`.
- `is_single_pass_read` in `vllm/utils/diffusion.py` is the one eligibility rule. The scheduler uses it to attach the canvas. The sampler uses it to seed the canvas into the draft tokens when the request is added. The two always agree.
- The DiffusionGemma model state splits each fused request into a causal prompt row and a bidirectional canvas row on the same block table. Self-conditioning covers only the canvas rows. The sampler moves fused requests out of the encoder phase in the same step.

Tradeoffs:

- Outputs are not bit-identical with the flag on, which is why it is off by default. The README tells users to validate on their workload first.
- An eligible read waits until the free KV cache holds its prompt and canvas, rather than falling back to two steps.

Limitations:

- CPU only, which is where the fused pass was measured and validated.
- No CI job runs a fused forward pass of the model. `TestFusedAttention` checks the fused attention against two passes on the CPU kernel, in the CPU CI job.
- #60663 batches self-conditioning on the assumption that a request's whole query span is its canvas. A fused request's span also holds the end of its prompt. Whichever PR lands second has to start the canvas at `end - num_logits`.

The JevBench results confirm a real speedup (~20% faster, 228/231 items improved). Each read saves 0.11–0.17 s across prompt lengths, in line with the PR's 0.12–0.17 s, and the concurrency-4 run finishes 12% sooner. Please feel free to ask follow up questions if something looks off or incorrect. **Summary** - **Speed:** serial median time per decision drops from 681 to 545 ms (−20%). A repeat of flag off stays within ±5% of itself on 90% of items. At concurrency 4 the median drops from 1,891 to 1,265 ms. - **Quality:** with the flag off, this PR is bit-identical to `main`. With the flag on, accuracy and Intelligence stay within one item of flag off. 4 hard-tier decisions change serially and 7 at concurrency 4, in both directions, about as many as reading the flag-off server at concurrency 4 instead of serially (3). - **fp32:** the flag changes no decisions, and serial shifts drop from 14.6 pp to 0.07 pp. The bf16 decision changes come from rounding on near-tie items. **Accuracy and Intelligence (bf16, 231 items)** | arm | serial accuracy | serial Intelligence | concurrency 4 accuracy | concurrency 4 Intelligence | |---|---|---|---|---| | `main` | 83.98% | 78.9 | 84.42% | 79.4 | | flag off | 83.98% | 78.9 | 84.42% | 79.4 | | flag off, repeat | 83.98% | 78.9 | 84.42% | 79.4 | | flag on | 84.85% | 80.0 | 83.55% | 78.3 | **Paired per-item comparison (bf16, 231 items)** | comparison | changed decisions | correct→incorrect | incorrect→correct | mean shift | max shift | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | `main` vs flag off, serial | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | flag off repeat vs flag off, both phases | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | flag on vs off, serial | 4 | 1 | 3 | 2.30 pp | 43.1 pp | | flag on vs off, concurrency 4 | 7 | 4 | 2 | 2.49 pp | 41.9 pp | | control: flag off, concurrency 4 vs serial | 3 | 1 | 2 | 2.65 pp | 59.2 pp | **fp32 check (23 items)** These are the 23 items whose decision changed in either phase, plus the largest shifts. They were rerun with `--dtype float32`, with bf16 arms on the same items as a control. | comparison | changed decisions | mean shift | max shift | |---|---|---|---| | fp32 flag on vs off, serial | 0 | 0.07 pp | 0.92 pp | | fp32 flag on vs off, concurrency 4 | 0 | 0.45 pp | 9.37 pp | | control: fp32 flag off, concurrency 4 vs serial | 0 | 0.08 pp | 0.95 pp | | bf16 flag on vs off, serial | 4 | 14.55 pp | 43.08 pp | | bf16 flag on vs off, concurrency 4 | 5 | 10.33 pp | 26.14 pp | - The bf16 control arms reproduce the first run bit for bit on all 46 serial reads. - In fp32 the flag shifts items about as much as fp32 batching does, about four orders of magnitude less in log probability than in bf16. This is consistent with kernels rounding differently when a step's token count changes, not with a different computation. - One read is still open. `hard-opus-c-long_policy-03` (3,493 tokens) moved 9.4 pp with the flag on at concurrency 4, and its decision did not change. It was submitted with three other prompts of 3,300 to 3,600 tokens, which forces chunked prefill.
